title: Real-time leaderboard: cache the top, rank in memory
brief: Design the leaderboard for a mobile game: players post scores, and everyone sees the live top 100 and their own rank. In SQL the reads are ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 100 and a COUNT of players above you, and every score update has to keep those answers current.

requirements: 100k rps, 99% reads (1k score updates/s): a world final, millions watching
90% of reads are the top-100 list: the same for every player, may be 2 s stale
variants.twist: Every screen now shows the player's own rank too, and that is different for each player, so no shared copy can answer it. Lower the CDN (or front cache) hit_ratio to 0.5 and run again. What breaks behind it, and what store answers 'my rank' without counting rows?

requirements: 30k rps, 70% score updates (21k/s): a live tournament, every match posts scores
Reads (top 100 and 'my rank') must reflect updates within 1 s
variants.twist: Season finale: set_traffic(rps=150000). One sorted set lives on one node. When you split it across nodes, by what key? How do you still answer the global top 100, and a player's exact rank? Two players with the same score: who ranks first? (The sim spreads load evenly over a store's replicas and can't model cross-shard rank or ties: talk it through.)

hints: How many score updates per second does each variant send, and how many writes per second can one SQL primary take? Which reads get the same answer for every player?

The top 100 is one answer shared by everyone, so a copy at the edge or in a cache can serve it. Score updates can't be cached: at tens of thousands per second, the store itself has to keep scores sorted, in memory.

Spectators: client -> CDN (hit 0.9) -> LB -> about 12-15 services -> cache (hit 0.9) -> SQL DB. Tournament: no cache helps; put an in-memory sorted store (one node, like a sorted set with ZADD / ZRANGE ... REV / ZREVRANK) behind about 33-35 services instead of the SQL DB.
_notes: The sim has no per-query cost, so a ranking query costs SQL the same as any query (5k/s per node); the lesson turns on the write rate. Spectators: 99k reads + 1k writes. Naive client -> service -> SQL: p99 ~5184 ms, 98% errors. Without a CDN the LB (50k) and ~100 services are the wall: 3 LBs + 110 services + Redis carries it but costs $11.31. CDN hit 0.9 x read share 0.99 = 0.89, so origin gets ~10.9k. CDN + 12 services + SQL alone: DB rho 2.35, fails. CDN + cache (hit 0.9) + SQL: DB rho 0.56, p99 ~60 ms / $1.98 at 12 services, ~53 ms / $2.08 at 13. CDN + 12 + Redis as the store also passes ($1.55). CDN + 12 + SQL with 2 read replicas carries it but costs $2.83. Tournament: 9k reads + 21k writes. Naive: p99 ~5184 ms, 94% errors. 35 services + SQL: DB rho 7.0. CDN + cache + SQL still fails (writes pass through, DB rho 5.19). 33 or 34 services + Redis (100k/node, rho 0.30): p99 ~54 ms / $3.55 at 33 services, ~43 ms / $3.65 at 34. The generic cache ($3.58) and Valkey ($3.61) pass too: accept any in-memory sorted structure. Over-provisioned: 7 SQL shards behind a router carry it (rho 0.86) but cost $6.96; Redis with 4 nodes costs $4.31. A plain KV (3 nodes, 34 services) sits at rho 1.00 and costs $4.33, but CDN + 26 services + KV passes at $3.63: the sim can't tell a sorted set from a hash, so ask how a KV would answer 'my rank' (it can't without a scan or a separate sorted index). Cross-shard rank and ties are talk-through only. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
